mainTopic: Fasting on the days around פורים, the stories of יום ניקנור and יום טוריינוס, the end of the chapter, and emergencies that call for an immediate outcry
overview: The גמרא asks which early-reading case the משנה means when it says fasting and הספד are still allowed. It rules out the 14th, the 13th (יום ניקנור) and the 12th (יום טוריינוס), and challenges that it must mean the 11th, the day before יום טוריינוס. It answers that the משנה means the 12th after all, because יום טוריינוס was cancelled when שמעיה and his brother אחיה were killed on it, as רב נחמן also ruled. רב אשי adds that a cancelled day is not restricted again just because יום ניקנור comes next. The גמרא then tells the stories behind both days: the defeat of the Greek general ניקנור, and the death of טוריינוס right after he killed לוליינוס and פפוס. Back to the משנה, רב אחא and רבי אסי argue about how many fasts count as a 'beginning'. The הלכה follows חכמים: such a fast is kept and completed. The chapter ends with הדרן, and a new משנה teaches that sick plants, long gaps between rains, weak rain, or a city left dry call for crying out immediately.

steps.title: When does the משנה allow fasting and eulogizing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת מגילה about reading early (fasting and הספד are allowed) and asks which case it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says they are allowed to eulogize and fast. When is this talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes words from a משנה in מסכת מגילה about towns that read the מגילה early (brought here as a test case, not the Taanit משנה) and asks which case they mean. This sets up a search through the possible days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that even when the מגילה is read early, הספד and תענית are still allowed on those days. The גמרא wants to find the exact case, because some of these days are already holidays where fasting is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A eulogy; mourning words for someone who passed away

phrases.english: They are permitted to eulogize and to fast.
When?

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּתָּרִין בְּהֶסְפֵּד וְתַעֲנִית. אֵימַת?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the analysis of the quoted משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which early-reading day the משנה means when it permits הספד and תענית.

steps.title: Not walled cities reading on the fourteenth
steps.stepSummary: First guess: people who normally read on the 15th read on the 14th instead. The גמרא asks how fasting could be allowed then.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means people who normally read on the fifteenth, and this time they read on the fourteenth, is fasting really allowed then?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first case: walled cities (who read on the 15th) reading on the 14th. Then it asks whether fasting is even allowed on that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 14th is פורים for regular towns, so it is not a plain day for anyone. The question 'is it permitted?' signals that fasting on the 14th is forbidden even for walled cities. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offers a possibility that will be tested)
People of the fifteenth: walled cities that read the מגילה on the 15th of Adar
But is it permitted? (a challenge, not a real question)

phrases.english: If you say it means those of the fifteenth
and they read it on the fourteenth,
but is it permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא בְּנֵי חֲמֵיסַר וְקָא קָרוּ לֵיהּ בְּאַרְבֵּיסַר, וּמִי שְׁרֵי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the first possible answer to the question and challenges it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The case of walled cities reading on the 14th.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Fasting is not allowed on the 14th even for walled cities.

steps.title: Proof from מגילת תענית and רבא
steps.stepSummary: מגילת תענית forbids eulogizing on the 14th and 15th, and רבא explains that this applies to each type of city on the other's day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written in מגילת תענית: the fourteenth and fifteenth of אדר are days of פורים, and one may not eulogize on them. רבא said: this was needed only to forbid each group on the other group's day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof for the challenge: מגילת תענית forbids eulogizing on both days, and רבא explains why that was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each group's own פורים day is already known from the פסוק, so מגילת תענית adds something new. רבא says the news is that walled cities may not eulogize on the 14th, and regular towns may not eulogize on the 15th. So walled cities reading on the 14th could never fast that day, and the משנה cannot mean that case.

keyTerms.meaning: An early list of happy days on which fasting and eulogizing are forbidden
It was needed only for... (shows what new thing a source teaches)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not mean each group celebrates both days. He only means each group may not fast or eulogize on the other group's day.

phrases.english: But isn't it written in מגילת תענית:
the fourteenth day of it
and the fifteenth day of it,
phrases.notes: 'Of it' means of the month of Adar.

phrases.english: they are the days of פורים
on which one may not eulogize.
And רבא said: it was not needed,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לֶאֱסוֹר אֶת שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה
phrases.english: except to forbid those of this one on that day
phrases.notes: Walled-city people may not eulogize on the 14th, the day of the regular towns.

phrases.english: and those of that one on this day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב בִּמְגִילַּת תַּעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source proving the challenge in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That walled cities may not fast or eulogize on the 14th.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מגילת תענית, as explained by רבא.

steps.title: Not the thirteenth, because it is יום ניקנור
steps.stepSummary: Second guess: people of the 14th read on the 13th. That day is יום ניקנור, so fasting is already forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it means people of the fourteenth who read on the thirteenth. But that is יום ניקנור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second case, reading on the 13th, and quickly rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 13th of אדר is יום ניקנור, its own happy day where fasting is not allowed. So the משנה could not be permitting fasting on the 13th.

keyTerms.meaning: People of the fourteenth: regular towns that read on the 14th
The 13th of Adar, a celebration day listed in מגילת תענית

phrases.english: But rather, those of the fourteenth
who read it on the thirteenth —
it is יום ניקנור!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא, בְּנֵי אַרְבֵּיסַר וְקָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ בִּתְלֵיסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first guess failed, offers a second guess and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The case of reading on the 13th.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 13th is יום ניקנור, when fasting is already forbidden.

steps.title: Not the twelfth, because it is יום טוריינוס
steps.stepSummary: Third guess: people of the 14th read on the 12th. That day is יום טוריינוס, also a day when fasting is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it means people of the fourteenth who read on the twelfth. But that is יום טוריינוס!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries reading on the 12th and rejects it for the same kind of reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 12th of אדר is יום טוריינוס, another happy day where fasting is not allowed. This leaves only one early day to check: the 11th.

keyTerms.meaning: The 12th of Adar, a celebration day listed in מגילת תענית

phrases.english: But rather, those of the fourteenth
who read it on the twelfth —
it is יום טוריינוס!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא, בְּנֵי אַרְבֵּיסַר וְקָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ בִּתְרֵיסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third guess, built the same way as step 4, and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The case of reading on the 12th.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 12th is יום טוריינוס, when fasting is already forbidden.

steps.title: It must be the eleventh, and the משנה still permits fasting
steps.stepSummary: Only the 11th is left, the day before יום טוריינוס, and the משנה permits fasting and הספד on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So isn't it talking about people who read on the eleventh? And the משנה teaches that eulogizing and fasting are permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: Having ruled out every other day, the גמרא concludes the משנה means reading on the 11th, and it allows fasting there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 11th is the day right before יום טוריינוס, a holiday from מגילת תענית. Since the unnamed משנה allows fasting on it, it holds that fasting is allowed on the day before such a holiday. This becomes a challenge for anyone who holds that fasting on the day before is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it...? (introduces the only remaining option)
And it teaches (points back to what the משנה says)

steps.whatToRemember: By ruling out the 14th, 13th and 12th, the גמרא proves the משנה is talking about the 11th. So the unnamed משנה permits fasting on the day before יום טוריינוס.
steps.whyThisMatters: This inference is the basis for asking whether the unnamed משנה conflicts with the view that the day before a מגילת תענית holiday is forbidden for fasting.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו, דְּקָא קָרוּ לֵיהּ בַּחֲדֵיסַר,
phrases.english: Rather, isn't it where they read it on the eleventh,
and it teaches that eulogizing and fasting are permitted!
phrases.notes: The 11th is the day right before יום טוריינוס, and that is the point.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, דְּקָא קָרוּ לֵיהּ בַּחֲדֵיסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After every other option was ruled out, settles on the 11th and draws the inference.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The unnamed משנה allows fasting and הספד on the 11th of Adar, the day before יום טוריינוס.

steps.title: Back to the 12th: יום טוריינוס was cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the answer that the משנה means the 11th. It goes back to the 12th and explains that יום טוריינוס is no longer a festive day.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The משנה is talking about people who normally read on the 14th but read that year on the 12th. And as for what you said, that the 12th is יום טוריינוס: יום טוריינוס itself was cancelled, because שמעיה and his brother אחיה were killed on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'No' to the answer of the 11th and goes back to the 12th. It removes the objection by explaining that יום טוריינוס is no longer kept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, the 12th was rejected only because it was יום טוריינוס, a day when fasting is not allowed. Now the גמרא says that day was cancelled because two righteous brothers were killed on it. So that objection disappears, and the 12th works again.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 6's argument for the 11th was only a challenge. Here the גמרא rejects it and says the משנה means the 12th.

phrases.english: No, it means people of the fourteenth,
who read it on the twelfth.
And as for what you said, that it is Trajan's Day:
Trajan's Day itself was cancelled,
since there were killed on it
Shemaya and his brother Achiya.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, בְּנֵי אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר, וְקָא קָרוּ לֵיהּ בִּתְרֵיסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by bringing back the guess from step 5 and removing the objection made there.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes the objection: the problem day is no longer kept.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 12th could not be the משנה's case because יום טוריינוס forbids fasting.
steps.terutzMaskana: יום טוריינוס was cancelled, so fasting on the 12th is allowed and the משנה can mean the 12th.

steps.title: רב נחמן fasted on the 12th
steps.stepSummary: A story shows that יום טוריינוס was really cancelled. רב נחמן called a fast on the 12th and defended it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the case of רב נחמן, who called a fast on the 12th. The rabbis said to him: 'It is יום טוריינוס!' He told them: 'יום טוריינוס itself was cancelled, because שמעיה and his brother אחיה were killed on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the last step with a real case. רב נחמן declared a fast on the 12th and gave the same reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim that יום טוריינוס was cancelled is not just a theory to answer a question. It was put into practice: an אמורא actually fasted on that day and answered the other rabbis' objection with this exact reason.

phrases.english: Like this case of Rav Nachman,
who declared a fast on the twelfth;
the rabbis said to him:
It is Trajan's Day!
He said to them:
Trajan's Day itself was cancelled,
since there were killed on it
Shemaya and his brother Achiya.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב נַחְמָן גְּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא בִּתְרֵיסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 7 with a real case.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that יום טוריינוס was cancelled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן declared a fast on the 12th and gave this reason.

steps.title: But the 12th is the day before יום ניקנור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why fasting on the 12th is not forbidden anyway, since it is the day before יום ניקנור.
steps.simpleTranslation: But fasting on the 12th should be forbidden anyway, because it is the day before יום ניקנור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with fasting on the 12th, even after יום טוריינוס was cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said the 13th is יום ניקנור. Days close to a festive day can also be restricted, so the 12th should be off-limits for fasting as the day before it, whether or not יום טוריינוס still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: let him get it from a different reason

phrases.english: But let him get it from
phrases.notes: The גמרא means: you don't even need יום טוריינוס. There's another reason fasting should be forbidden.

phrases.english: the fact that it is the day before Nicanor's Day!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ יוֹם שֶׁלִּפְנֵי נִיקָנוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of steps 7-8 that fasting on the 12th is allowed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that fasting on the 12th is allowed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 12th is the day before יום ניקנור, so fasting should be forbidden for that reason.

steps.title: רב אשי: no new restriction because of the next day
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that since יום טוריינוס itself was cancelled, the rabbis would not forbid fasting on it only because יום ניקנור comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Now that the day itself was cancelled, should we go and make a new rule against fasting on it because of יום ניקנור?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question about the day before יום ניקנור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rabbis deliberately took away this day's special status. It would make no sense to give it back a restriction only because it sits next to יום ניקנור. Once the day was cancelled, it became a regular day.

keyTerms.meaning: should we go and make a rule?

steps.whatToRemember: The 12th of אדר is a permitted fast day: יום טוריינוס was cancelled, and being the day before יום ניקנור does not forbid it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Now that it itself was cancelled,
because of Nicanor's Day
should we go and make a decree?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הַשְׁתָּא אִיהוּ גּוּפֵיהּ בַּטְּלוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical answer: a cancelled day is not given a new restriction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The day before יום ניקנור should forbid fasting.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the rabbis cancelled יום טוריינוס, they would not restrict it again because of the next day.

steps.title: What are יום ניקנור and יום טוריינוס?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the stories behind these two days.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is ניקנור, and what is טוריינוס?
steps.whatsHappening: The discussion turns to background. The גמרא asks what happened on these two days, which sets up the stories that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question does not attack anything. It asks for information about the two days the argument has been using.

phrases.english: What is Nicanor
and what is Trajan?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי נִיקָנוֹר וּמַאי טוּרְיָינוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a background section about the days mentioned in the discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What events these two days remember.

steps.title: The story of ניקנור
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how ניקנור threatened ירושלים and how the חשמונאים defeated him and hung his thumbs and big toes on the city gates.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: ניקנור was one of the Greek generals. Every single day he would wave his hand over יהודה and ירושלים and say, 'When will it fall into my hands so I can trample it?' When the kingdom of the חשמונאים grew strong and defeated them, they cut off his thumbs and big toes and hung them on the gates of ירושלים. They said: 'The mouth that spoke so proudly, and the hands that waved over ירושלים, let vengeance be done to them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first half of the question with a ברייתא about ניקנור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ניקנור boasted every day that he would destroy ירושלים. When the חשמונאים won, they punished him in a way that matched his arrogance, which is why his defeat became a day of celebration.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
Nicanor was one of the Greek generals,
and every single day

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה מֵנִיף יָדוֹ עַל יְהוּדָה וִירוּשָׁלַיִם,
phrases.english: he would wave his hand over Judea and Jerusalem
and say: When will it fall into my hands so I can trample it?
And when the Hasmonean kingdom grew strong
and defeated them,
they cut off his thumbs and big toes
and hung them on the gates of Jerusalem,
and said: The mouth that spoke with pride,
and the hands that waved over Jerusalem:
let vengeance be done to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: נִיקָנוֹר, אֶחָד מֵאִפַּרְכֵי יְוָונִים הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ניקנור half of the question in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יום ניקנור celebrates the חשמונאים' defeat of the arrogant Greek general ניקנור.

steps.title: The story of טוריינוס begins
steps.stepSummary: טוריינוס mocked לוליינוס and פפוס, saying their God should save them as He saved חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה. They replied that those were complete צדיקים and נבוכדנצר was a fitting king for a miracle.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is טוריינוס? They said: When טוריינוס wanted to kill לוליינוס and his brother פפוס in לודקיא, he said to them: 'If you are from the people of חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה, let your God come and save you from my hand, the way He saved חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה from the hand of נבוכדנצר!' They said to him: 'חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה were complete צדיקים, and they deserved to have a miracle done for them. And נבוכדנצר was a proper king, and it was fitting for a miracle to happen through him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now answers the second half of the question: the story behind יום טוריינוס. The story continues in steps 14-16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers explain why no miracle should be expected for them. The people saved in the past were complete צדיקים, and the king involved was worthy of having a miracle happen through him. They are humbly saying that neither condition applies now.

keyTerms.meaning: the three saved from נבוכדנצר's furnace

phrases.english: What is Trajan? They said:
When Trajan wanted to kill
Luleyanus and his brother Pappus in Laodicea,
he said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אִם מֵעַמּוֹ שֶׁל חֲנַנְיָה מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה אַתֶּם —
phrases.english: If you are from the people of Chananya, Mishael, and Azarya,
let your God come and save you from my hand,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁהִצִּיל אֶת חֲנַנְיָה מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: the way He saved Chananya, Mishael, and Azarya
from the hand of Nebuchadnezzar!
phrases.notes: This refers to the furnace story in דניאל 3.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: חֲנַנְיָה מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִין הָיוּ,
phrases.english: Chananya, Mishael, and Azarya were completely righteous,
and they were worthy of having a miracle done for them.
And Nebuchadnezzar was a proper king,
and it was fitting for a miracle to be done through him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טוּרְיָינוֹס? אָמְרוּ: כְּשֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ טוּרְיָינוֹס לַהֲרוֹג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the טוריינוס half of the question in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Begins the story of טוריינוס and the brothers לוליינוס and פפוס. The story continues in steps 14-16.

steps.title: טוריינוס is not worthy of a miracle
steps.stepSummary: לוליינוס and פפוס finish their comparison: נבוכדנצר was a real king, but טוריינוס is just a commoner, so no miracle would be done through him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this wicked man is a commoner, and it is not right for a miracle to happen through him.
steps.whatsHappening: לוליינוס and פפוס finish answering טוריינוס's mocking. They explain why they should not expect a miracle like the one done for חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13 they said נבוכדנצר was a fitting king for a miracle. Now they give the other half of the comparison: טוריינוס is a nobody. A great miracle is not done through such a person.

keyTerms.meaning: A commoner, an ordinary person, not a real king

phrases.english: But that wicked man is a commoner,
phrases.notes: They mean טוריינוס, the one talking to them. They are comparing him to נבוכדנצר from the step before.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ רָאוּי לַעֲשׂוֹת נֵס עַל יָדוֹ.
phrases.english: and it is not fitting for a miracle to be done through him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע, הֶדְיוֹט הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided comparison started in step 13 (worthy people and a worthy king, against unworthy people and an unworthy king).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No miracle should be expected, because טוריינוס is not a king fitting for a miracle.

steps.title: ה׳ has many ways to punish us, but He will avenge our blood
steps.stepSummary: The two brothers say they deserve death from ה׳ for their sins. ה׳ could have used many messengers. He handed them to טוריינוס only so He could later punish him for killing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already deserve destruction from ה׳. If you do not kill us, ה׳ has many other killers, and many bears and lions that can attack and kill us. ה׳ gave us into your hands only so that He will later make you pay for our blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The brothers continue speaking. They explain that their death does not prove ה׳ cannot save them. Instead, it will bring punishment on טוריינוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They admit they are not complete צדיקים like חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה, so they deserve punishment. Since ה׳ has countless ways to carry it out, choosing טוריינוס has a purpose: he becomes guilty and will be punished. This sets up the end of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: A name for ה׳, literally 'the Place'

phrases.english: And we have become deserving of destruction before ה׳,
and if you do not kill us,
ה׳ has many killers,
and many bears and lions
does ה׳ have in His world
that could attack us and kill us.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, לֹא מְסָרָנוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּיָדְךָ,
phrases.english: Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave us into your hand
only because He will in the future make you pay for our blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָנוּ נִתְחַיַּיבְנוּ כְּלָיָה לַמָּקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the brothers' reply. Having explained why no miracle comes, they now explain what their death really means.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Their death is deserved for their own sins, but טוריינוס was chosen as the killer so that he will be punished for it.

steps.title: טוריינוס kills them and is killed himself
steps.stepSummary: טוריינוס kills the brothers right away. Before people even left the place, two officers came from רומי and smashed his skull with clubs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, he killed them immediately. They said: people had not yet moved from there when two officers came from רומי and split his skull with clubs.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. The brothers' words come true quickly: טוריינוס is punished right after he kills them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes the answer to step 11's question about where יום טוריינוס comes from. The quick punishment of טוריינוס was seen as ה׳ avenging their blood, and that day became a day of celebration.

keyTerms.meaning: Even so, in spite of this

steps.whatToRemember: יום טוריינוס marks the day טוריינוס was killed right after killing לוליינוס and פפוס, just as they said ה׳ would avenge their blood.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן הֲרָגָן מִיָּד.
phrases.english: Even so, he killed them immediately.
They said: they had not moved from there
before two officers came from Rome
and split his skull with clubs.
phrases.notes: 'His' means טוריינוס. Literally it says they 'wounded his brain'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן הֲרָגָן מִיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the brothers' prediction coming true and closes the story begun in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יום טוריינוס celebrates the death of טוריינוס, who was killed right after he murdered לוליינוס and פפוס.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: no starting fasts on Thursday or ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה again: a public fast is not first set on a Thursday, and fasts are not set on ראש חודש and similar days.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not first set a public fast on a Thursday, etc. We do not set a fast on ראש חודש, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the stories and goes back to quoting the משנה. This is a setup line for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה, which says that if a series of fasts already began, it is not stopped for these days. The next step asks what counts as having 'begun'.

keyTerms.meaning: At the start, as the first fast

phrases.english: We do not set a fast on the community
starting on a Thursday, etc.,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין גּוֹזְרִין תַּעֲנִית בְּרָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: we do not set a fast on New Moons, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: if the fasts already began, they are not stopped for these days. The next question depends on this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין גּוֹזְרִין תַּעֲנִית עַל הַצִּבּוּר בַּתְּחִלָּה בַּחֲמִישִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories about the festive days and returns to explaining the משנה's rules about fasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A public fast series does not begin on Thursday or on ראש חודש and similar days, but an existing series is not interrupted.

steps.title: How many fasts count as a beginning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how many fasts must already have been kept for the series to count as 'begun'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how many fasts count as a beginning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the משנה: what is the minimum number of fasts before the series counts as already started?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that a series that has already begun is not stopped for ראש חודש and the like. But the משנה did not say how many fasts make a 'beginning', so the גמרא asks.

phrases.english: And how many count as a beginning?
phrases.notes: He means how many fasts must already be kept before the festive day for the series to count as started.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה הָוְיָא הַתְחָלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of a word implied in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum number of fasts kept before a festive day for the series to continue on that day.

steps.title: רב אחא says three, רבי אסי says one
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא says a beginning is three fasts. רבי אסי says even one fast is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא said: three. רבי אסי said: one.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question with different numbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב אחא, the series is not continued on a festive day unless three fasts were already kept. According to רבי אסי, keeping even one fast is enough to count as a beginning. The גמרא does not decide between them here.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa said: three.
Rabbi Asi said: one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא אָמַר: שָׁלֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two competing answers to the question in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A dispute: three fasts according to רב אחא, one fast according to רבי אסי.

steps.title: This is רבי מאיר's view; חכמים say fast and finish
steps.stepSummary: רב says the משנה's ruling, that such a fast is not finished, follows רבי מאיר quoting רבן גמליאל. חכמים say one fasts and completes the fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This is the view of רבי מאיר, who said it in the name of רבן גמליאל. But חכמים say: one fasts and completes the fast.
steps.whatsHappening: רב tells us that the משנה's ruling here is only one opinion, and that חכמים disagree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר quotes רבן גמליאל as saying that a fast continuing onto a festive day is kept but not finished until night. רב reveals that חכמים argue: the fast is kept all the way to the end of the day.

keyTerms.meaning: One fasts and completes the fast until night

steps.confusionAlert: 'זו' (this) is not about the number of fasts from step 19. It points back to the משנה's ruling about not finishing a fast that falls on a festive day.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
This is the statement of Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the משנה's ruling that a fast falling on such a festive day is kept but not finished.

phrases.english: who said it in the name of Rabban Gamliel,
but the Rabbis say: one fasts and completes the fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה and shows that its ruling about not completing the fast is disputed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not finishing such a fast is the view of רבי מאיר quoting רבן גמליאל; חכמים say one fasts and completes it.

steps.title: The הלכה: fast and complete the fast
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא taught in the name of רב הונא that the halacha follows חכמים: one fasts and completes the fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא taught in the name of רב הונא: The halacha is that one fasts and completes the fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling on the dispute from the step before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there is a dispute between רבי מאיר and חכמים, we need to know which view to follow. רב הונא rules like חכמים: a fast series that runs into a festive day is kept all the way until night.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows חכמים: if a fast series reaches a festive day like ראש חודש, one fasts and finishes the fast until night.

phrases.aramaic: דָּרֵשׁ מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra taught publicly in the name of Rav Huna:
The halakha is: one fasts and completes the fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא: הֲלָכָה מִתְעַנֶּה וּמַשְׁלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute presented in step 20 in favor of חכמים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The halacha is like חכמים: one fasts and completes the fast.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter סדר תעניות כיצד
steps.stepSummary: The chapter סדר תעניות כיצד ends with the traditional הדרן closing line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'סדר תעניות כיצד'.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter that opened with the words 'סדר תעניות כיצד'. It is not part of the argument. It is a closing formula, and a new chapter starts right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion of fasts for rain, including the last ruling that one fasts and completes the fast, is now finished for this chapter. Saying הדרן shows love for the learning and a promise to come back to it.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a chapter)
A chapter of the משנה and גמרא

steps.whatToRemember: The chapter on the order of fasts for rain is now complete. The הלכה we ended on: one who fasts on such a day completes the fast, like the חכמים.

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'The order of fasts, how?'
phrases.notes: 'סדר תעניות כיצד' is the name of the chapter we just finished, taken from its first words.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter right after the final halachic ruling in step 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter סדר תעניות כיצד is complete.

steps.title: New משנה: the slow order of fasts is only for a late first rain
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter's משנה says the step-by-step series of fasts is only for when the first rainfall is late. Sick-looking plants, or a forty-day break between rains, call for crying out right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: The order of fasts we learned applies when the first rainfall did not come. But if plants changed and look sick, they cry out right away. And likewise, if the rain stopped for forty days between one rainfall and the next, they cry out, because that is a plague of drought.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה. It limits the slow, step-by-step order of fasts from the first chapter to one case, a late first rain, and lists emergencies where the community cries out immediately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier chapter the fasts got harder one stage at a time, with waiting between them. This משנה says that slow approach fits only a delayed first rain. When damage is already showing, like sick plants or a forty-day dry spell, there is no waiting. The forty-day gap is called a real 'plague of drought'.

keyTerms.meaning: The first rainfall of the rainy season
They cry out or sound the alarm (prayer, fasting, blowing)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as cancelling the order of fasts. That order still holds for a late first rain. This משנה only adds emergency cases that skip the waiting.

phrases.english: The order of these fasts
phrases.notes: He means the fasts that get harder step by step, which we learned in the last chapter.

phrases.english: is stated for the first rainfall.
But plants that changed
phrases.notes: Literally 'that changed'. The plants grew but now look sick or damaged.

phrases.english: they cry out about them immediately.
And likewise, if the rains stopped
between one rain and the next for forty days
they cry out about them,
because it is a plague of drought.

steps.triggerLanguage: סֵדֶר תַּעֲנִיּוֹת אֵלּוּ הָאָמוּר בִּרְבִיעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter after the הדרן, looking back at the order of fasts from the first chapter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gradual order of fasts applies only to a delayed first rain. Sick plants or a forty-day gap between rains call for crying out immediately.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the main idea of the new chapter: urgent, visible damage calls for immediate public prayer, not the slow build-up of fasts.

steps.title: More emergencies: rain that is not enough, and a city left dry
steps.stepSummary: The משנה goes on. If rain helped plants but not trees, trees but not plants, or both but did not fill the cisterns, they cry out right away. The same applies to a single city that got no rain, backed by a פסוק in עמוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: If rain fell enough for the plants but not for the trees, or for the trees but not for the plants, or for both but not enough to fill the cisterns, ditches and caves, they cry out right away. And likewise a city that got no rain, as it is written: 'I made it rain on one city, and on another city I did not make it rain; one field got rain...'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing cases that need an immediate outcry. This time the rain came but was not enough for every need, or skipped one city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain falling is not the whole story. It has to cover plants, trees, and the water stored for summer. If any one of these is missing, it counts as an emergency. A city skipped by the rain is treated as a sign of punishment, and the משנה proves this from the פסוק in עמוס.
steps.whatToRemember: An immediate outcry is needed not only when there is no rain, but also when rain is too weak for some need, plants, trees, or stored water, or when it skips one city.

phrases.aramaic: יָרְדוּ לַצְּמָחִין אֲבָל לֹא יָרְדוּ לָאִילָן,
phrases.english: If rain fell enough for the plants but did not fall enough for the trees,
for the trees but not for the plants,
for this one and that one,
phrases.notes: Meaning enough for both the plants and the trees.

phrases.english: but not for the cisterns, the ditches and the caves
they cry out about them immediately.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן עִיר שֶׁלֹּא יָרְדוּ עָלֶיהָ גְּשָׁמִים,
phrases.english: And likewise a city on which rain did not fall,
as it is written: 'And I made it rain on one city,'
'and on another city I did not make it rain;'
'one field will get rain, etc.'
phrases.notes: The rest of the פסוק says the field that got no rain dries up.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָרְדוּ לַצְּמָחִין אֲבָל לֹא יָרְדוּ לָאִילָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of emergencies, moving from a lack of rain to rain that is not enough or misses one city.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain that is not enough for plants, trees, or stored water, or that skips one city, calls for an immediate outcry.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עמוס 4:7, showing that rain falling on one city but not another is a punishment from Above.
